objective.statement: Write the scales and key signatures of B major and G sharp minor, with a double sharp where it is needed.
successCriteria: I know B major and G♯ minor have five sharps.
I can write both scales, ascending and descending, with accidentals.
I know why G♯ minor needs F𝄪 and cannot use G instead.

explanation.text: Grade 4 adds four new keys, each with five sharps or flats. The two 'sharp' keys are B major and its relative minor, G♯ minor. Five sharps are F♯, C♯, G♯, D♯ and A♯, in that order. For a sharp key the major tonic is a semitone above the last sharp: A♯ is the last, so the key is B major.

music.textAlternative: A treble-clef stave with eight semibreves: the B major scale, ascending, written with accidentals instead of a key signature.

explanation.caption: B major, ascending, written with accidentals instead of a key signature.

explanation.text: A key signature and an accidental both alter notes, but differently. A key signature at the start of the line alters every note of that letter, in every octave, for the whole piece. An accidental beside a note alters that note, and any later note of the same line or space, only until the barline. When you write a scale without a key signature, every altered note needs its own accidental.

G♯ minor has the same signature as B major. In the harmonic minor the 7th degree is raised by a semitone. The 7th of G♯ minor is F♯, which is already sharp in the key signature, so raising it makes F𝄪, a double sharp. You cannot write it as G natural, because the scale already has a G♯ as its first note, and every letter name must appear once, in order.

music.textAlternative: A treble-clef stave with eight semibreves: the G♯ harmonic minor scale, ascending, with its key signature.

explanation.caption: G♯ harmonic minor with its key signature: the F𝄪 is written as an accidental.

explanation.text: Five sharps: B major and G♯ minor. G♯ minor needs F𝄪 for its raised 7th (harmonic) and E♯ and F𝄪 going up in the melodic form; coming down the melodic minor returns to the key signature.

music.textAlternative: A treble-clef stave with eight semibreves: the G♯ melodic minor scale, ascending, written with accidentals instead of a key signature.

steps: Start on G♯. The first five notes follow the key signature: G♯ A♯ B C♯ D♯.
Going up, the melodic minor raises the 6th and 7th: E♯ and F𝄪.
Coming down, both return to the key signature: F♯ and E.

F#.reason: That is the 7th of the key signature (the natural minor). The harmonic minor raises the 7th by a semitone.

E.reason: That is the 6th degree. The leading note is the 7th, a semitone below the tonic.
